Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As controversy surrounding over an investigation into the Minister of Finance continues, CB asks what impact it is having on the SA economy

Summary:
A City Press article this past sunday alleges that the investigation into Minister of Finance Pravin Gordhan has been reopened and handed to the Crime Intelligence unit of the SAPS. Meanwhile the Hawks are denying that they are continuing with an investigation, and the Presidency is insisting that the so called "war" between Pres Zuma and the minister of finance is a toxic narrative peddled by local and foreign media. What effect is the saga having on SA's economy?

Further information:
Background Info: My Crime intelligence source was concerned about the info in the City Press article because Crime Intelligence does not have investigative capacity and would not want/need the docket which has apparently been handed to them. He will confirm today or early tomorrow whether the story is true but it is tricky, not the kind of thing he can just openly ask about so needs time. My SARS source is saying that he believes this is political maneuvering and pushing a "state capture" line. He says issues such as Gordhan's tirade against a JV deal BY Denel Asia and Gupta linked (Ajay Gupta's son is a director) VR Laser are putting him in Jacob Zuma's sights. Thw above is just for context.

We have confirmed interviews with Gwede Manatashe, Economist Thabi Leoka and Gareth Newham from the institute for security studies. We have also confirmed interview with Abram from City Press, and he has agreed to supply us with supporting docs for his story, which includes a briefing by Ntlemeze from the Hawks to Crimes against the state on the status of the investigation into the minister of finance at a time when the case against him was supposedly closed. We have also asked Aubrey Matshiqi for an interview to unpack the political story and S&P Global for comment following their release this friday of SA's ratings.

Press Release:


Pravin Probed
Is the insinuation that Jacob Zuma is engaged in a “war” with Minister of Finance Pravin Gordhan a “toxic narrative” peddled by the media? So says the Presidency. Yet controversial details around investigation into an alleged illicit spy unit within SARS and Minister Gordhan continue to emerge. With agency Standard & Poor’s to pronounce on the country’s credit rating this week, just what impact has such turbulence had on the economy? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Pravin Probed
4 June 2016

Voice
On Friday night news broke that South Africa had not been downgraded to junk status by ratings agency Standard and Poors. But slow economic growth means we are by no means safe from a credit rating downgrade.

Link Bongani
The news that South Africa has avoided another downgrade has been met with welcome relief. But it remains to be seen how long we can keep the wolves at bay.

Sound Up Thabi Leoka
I don’t think this is something to celebrate, I don’t think this is victory because S&P and Fitch are reviewing the country again in December.

Voice
Economist Thabi Leoka says it might be too late to avoid being downgraded by the end of the year.

Sound Up Thabi
This is still a very short time, 6 months, of reforming the country- making sure that GDP grows. Already the first quarter of GDP is still very slow actually, contraction. So I don’t expect us to be safe from another downgrade, we’re likely to be downgraded in December, if we’re continuing on at the same pace.

Voice
So at a time when the country is in desperate need of leadership allegations of state capture and reports of a continuing investigation into finance minister Pravin Gordhan are extremely worrying .

Sound Up Pravin Gordhan
…Allegations that are unfounded, based on leaked documents that even I have not seen…

Voice
Despite denials that the minister is under investigation, by both the Hawks and the Minister of Police, the headlines have not gone away.

Link Bongani
Hardly a week goes by without some explosive media report, from the alleged imminent arrest of the finance minister, to allegations of state capture. The presidency’s messaging has been consistent on this – denial, denial, denial. But is the evidence beginning to point towards a different direction?

Sound Up Abram Mashego
So what I needed was tangible evidence so that I could say – here is the proof. Then from there I started gathering the news.

Voice
Abram Mashego is a journalist with the City Press newspaper. Last Sunday the paper ran an article that alleged the case against Minister Gordhan had been reopened and handed to Crime Intelligence for further investigation.

Sound Up Abram
This case was opened at Brooklyn police station by Tom Moyane, and that was around May 2015.

Voice
Documents leaked to City Press from the police’s own case management system, show that case number 427/5/2015 was opened on the 16th of May last year. According to Abram the case was made by SARS commissioner Tom Moyane against his predecessor Ivan Pillay, SARS high risk investigations unit head Johann van Loggerenburg, and other SARS officials.

Sound Up Abram
Bongani: Now you also have a document to the Minister of State Security from Hawks head Berning Ntlemenza. What’s in it?

Abram: Inside the document, it outlines the case. It was sent in January. Ntlemenza then gave a briefing to the minister into what are they investigating that has Pravin Gordhan implicated into wrongdoing.

Bongani: So it specifically tells the State Security Minister that his cabinet colleague is a person of interest to the Hawks?

Abram: Correct

Voice
The case management system shows that the case was closed in December last year, well before the now infamous list of 27 questions was sent to minister Gordhan just days before his budget speech earlier this year, a move even questioned by the ruling party.

Sound Up Gwede Mantashe
We said: it is suspicious to send questions to the minister four days before the budget. That is what we said. And we said it is wrong to do that you are going to destabilize a very important process of presentation of the budget. We stand by that.

Voice
ANC Secretary General Gwede Mantashe says minister Gordhan has the full support of the party.

Sound Up Gwede
Minister Gordhan is the minister of finance, we have repeatedly said you have our support, the president came out and said you have our support, the NPA came out and said there is no prosecution against him, that is what we are taking as the ANC.

Voice
So if the Hawks were investigating Minister Gordhan after the case had been closed, the question is why?

Sound Up Gareth Newham
It will be very useful to know, and I’m sure if this ever gets to court this will come out, what was the basis for the Hawks to continue investigating.

Voice
Gareth Newham is the head of the Governance, Crime and Justice Division of the Institute for Security Studies. He says the public are right to question government’s denials of the investigation into the minister of finance.

Sound Up Gareth
The minister himself has said that there are people misusing the criminal justice system, who are undermining the country. So when very powerful people at the top of the political elite are telling us this, it suggests that there must be some truth to it.

Voice
According to the documents case 427 was reopened last week on the 25 May and the docket handed to Crime Intelligence.

Sound Up Gareth
They won’t necessarily hand over the entire docket to Crime Intelligence because Crime Intelligence won’t be the final structure that will hand over the docket to the NPA. But they have in this case so clearly they think that there is a lot of information that only Crime Intelligence have the resources to get on top of.

Voice
Crime Intelligence have not responded to our request for an interview on this matter. The Hawks, in a written response to Carte Blanche, said: “There is no investigation against the honourable Minister of Finance and we also distance ourselves from the malicious and unjustified reports”. The secrecy surrounding the case has fueled speculation of a on going battle between the heads of the presidency and the treasury.

Link Bongani
The presidency has dismissed any talk of a proxy war between President Zuma and Minister Gordahn, calling it a toxic narrative by the media. But all eyes remain on the highest office in the land to provide leadership on this matter.

Sound Up Aubrey Matshiqi
Unfortunately, if you look at what has been happening in our politics, in the ruling party and in the state, we have very serious deficits in honesty and the truth. The truth doesn’t matter. What matters are the ends to which you can put perceptions.

Voice
Political analyst Aubrey Matshiqi says we are witnessing the fall out of internal power struggles by members of the state and ruling party.

Sound Up Aubrey
We may wake up in a country, in fact we wake up in such a country as far as I’m concerned every day. A country where different sides in political battles inside the ANC and within the state manipulate state institutions in order to advantage their own positions.

Sound Up Gareth
We will not get on top of our big problems, solving of poverty and unemployment through growing the economy if the people who have the power to make the right decisions around that are fighting each other and engaged in proxy battles through the institutions of the criminal justice system. And that’s what the allegations are and certainly that means that most people just stop trusting these agencies and then we are on a slippery slope.

Voice
The City Press report comes at a time when the presidency and ruling party are fending off serious allegations of state capture, supposedly by members of the Gupta family. The allegations prompted the ANC to ask people to come forward with information.

Sound Up Gwede Mantashe
Eight people have come forward, we said please give us written submissions, we received one. And many of them said no we will not make written submissions.

Voice
Amongst the eight people was Deputy Finance Minister Mcebisi Jonas, who said members of the Gupta family had offered him the top job as minister of finance. But the ANC says they have put the matter to bed since they only received one written statement.

Sound Up Gwede
Bongani: The point I’m making is that if no less than deputy minister Jonas can publicly make these allegations and yet not make a written submission to you, you understand that it’s going to be difficult for others.

Gwede: Deputy minister Jonas is one of the eight, his statement is not something separate from the rest. Written submissions, not some affidavit, just written submission of your statement of facts, it’s not forthcoming, what do we do?

Sound Up Aubrey
There is a perception, or we are dealing with the reality, that state capture in South Africa is taking, amongst other things, the form of the president of the ruling party who has been captured by the Gupta’s.

Sound Up Gareth
At that level you really need a formal structure to investigate, one that is protected, ideally led by a judge, somebody who is completely independent and cannot be interfered with. That no one came forward to the ANC is not surprising we could have told Gwede Mantashe that from the beginning.

Link Bongani
With the local government elections just around the corner continued allegations of state capture couldn’t have come at a worse time for the ANC. But by putting the matter aside, is the party choosing it’s own unity above the interests of the country?

Voice
Aubrey says statements made by the likes of Baleka Mbethe who recently said that if the president were recalled there would be chaos in this country, make him more than just a little concerned.

Sound Up Aubrey
I want them to disabuse me of the notion that they are suggesting that both the ANC and the president will not go quietly if their political situation changes negatively. I hope that is not what they are suggesting.
